task_reconstruction.objective: Model multi-hop HF skywave path and energy over sea/ground, quantify hop/distance limits, and convert a frequency-band landing envelope into moving-ship reception time.
inputs: wind-driven sea state or ground Sh/material
task_reconstruction.decision: Choose a feasible frequency/angle/surface scenario and, for the moving ship, a bandwidth whose landing zones provide useful conditional coverage.

contributions.summary: Combines functional D/E/F layer roles with path and energy outputs in one named model.
Connects a piecewise electron-density profile to frequency-conditioned refractive index.
Uses an interpretable micro-element Snell march to produce a turning path and range.
Places a physical frequency-feasibility relation before propagation cases.
Extends calm-sea Fresnel reflection with a wind-driven roughness factor.
Reuses the reflection kernel with material replacement and a topographic correction.
Organizes sea and ground effects as paired baseline/perturbation cases.
Reports maximum hop count and distance across controlled frequency/angle cases.
Turns single-frequency landing points into bandwidth-generated intervals and residence time.
Explains significant and near-zero responses through visited state regions and affected subsystems.

edges.handoff: Functional E/F roles and default scenario parameterize the electron-density profile.
Ne(h) is converted to n(h,f).
The representative E-layer refractive index sets the F-entry angle.
The E-layer exit angle initializes F-layer marching.
The local refractive-index profile drives every F-layer Snell update.
Peak density and height feed the critical-frequency/MUF gate.
The physical feasibility limit should screen candidate carrier frequencies before recursion.
The calm-sea Fresnel coefficient is the baseline multiplied by roughness rho.
The rough-sea amplitude supplies per-reflection loss.
The smooth-ground Fresnel coefficient is reduced by the terrain factor.
The rugged-ground coefficient feeds the matched ground comparison.
D-layer attenuation enters the cumulative SNR ledger.
F-layer range and mirrored descent determine the hop geometry.
Accumulated path distance determines FSPL in the recursive ledger.
Frequency-specific noise initializes SNR0.
Terminal distance, hop count, SNR, and first-hop states feed result tables.
Repeated MHPM paths over a frequency band yield landing-point envelopes.
Each interval length is divided by ship speed.
E/F density and layer-height perturbations modify the refractive state.
Wind perturbations modify the rough-sea energy channel.
Sensitivity outputs qualify the baseline performance conclusions.

assumptions.summary: Retain D-layer attenuation, FSPL, and surface-reflection loss as the three propagation-energy components.
Treat the radio wave as a straight ray outside the refractive F-layer march and neglect divergence.
Treat the D layer as energy attenuation without path bending.
Compress the E layer to one refraction at a representative height.
Merge F1 and F2 into a refraction/reflection layer.
Use daytime summer conditions as the default profile.
Use 8 m/s as the representative wind unless a case overrides it.
Use 15 degrees as the default grazing angle unless otherwise specified.
Use 15, 17.65, and 20 MHz for comparative MHPM cases and 21-21.45 MHz for MSRSM.
Treat the sea as a locally flat homogeneous complex dielectric before roughness correction.
Represent smooth ground with wet-concrete material constants.
Represent rugged terrain by elevation standard deviation Sh.
Use a 200 Hz noise bandwidth and frequency-specific external noise values in printed code.
Use constant 41.67 km/h ship speed along the propagation-distance coordinate.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: Adopt N=1e10 m^-3 and collision rate 1e6 s^-1 for Equation 1.
Adopt E/F profile parameters from cited Sanya/Wuhan numerical studies.
Retain foE=3.21 MHz, hmE=101 km, ymE=10.7 km, foF2=14.20 MHz, hmF2=339.3 km, ymF2=78.0 km, NmE=10^10.5 m^-3, and NmF2=2.5e12 m^-3.
Use complex relative permittivity 70+i*300*lambda in the Fresnel model.
Use h=0.0051*v^2 as the effective wind-wave height interface.
Use eps_r=15 and sigma=0.05 S/m for wet concrete.
Use Sh in metres as the single rugged-ground descriptor.
Read external-noise factors from an ITU-derived frequency chart; code uses 27, 22, and 19 dB for 15, 17.65, and 20 MHz.
Hold non-target variables fixed across four calm/turbulent cases.
Hold frequency and angle fixed while varying Sh=5,10,15,20 m.
Bind bandwidth 21-21.45 MHz, 15 degrees, 20 m/s wind, and 41.67 km/h ship speed.
Perturb E/F peak density, F-layer height, and wind in separate deterministic sweeps.

models.summary: MU-A-2018-77845-001: D attenuates, E refracts once, and merged F bends/reflects the ray under a daytime-summer baseline.
MU-A-2018-77845-002: Electron density and collision rate produce a frequency-dependent attenuation coefficient.
MU-A-2018-77845-003: A four-piece profile joins an E parabola, linear bridge, F2 parabola, and topside exponential.
MU-A-2018-77845-004: The density profile becomes the refractive-index field used by E/F ray tracing.
MU-A-2018-77845-005: The continuous E layer is compressed to one interface at its representative height.
MU-A-2018-77845-006: A 0.01 km height march updates local angle and transverse distance until the ray becomes nearly horizontal.
MU-A-2018-77845-007: Peak density and Earth-radius geometry define an admissible reflection-frequency limit.
MU-A-2018-77845-008: A complex seawater permittivity and grazing angle produce polarization-specific coefficients.
MU-A-2018-77845-009: Wind speed determines effective wave height, roughness g, and multiplicative factor rho.
MU-A-2018-77845-010: Ground changes the complex permittivity inputs while preserving the polarization kernel.
MU-A-2018-77845-011: Frequency, grazing angle, and Sh define an exponential roughness penalty.
MU-A-2018-77845-012: Distance and carrier frequency enter the standard km/MHz FSPL form.
MU-A-2018-77845-013: Frequency-specific Fa values are added to thermal noise and subtracted from 100 W source power.
MU-A-2018-77845-014: One hop links E/F geometry, D absorption, FSPL, surface reflection, and an SNR continuation gate.
MU-A-2018-77845-015: Paired and controlled cases produce first-hop power, ratios, maximum hops, and distance.
MU-A-2018-77845-016: A continuous 21-21.45 MHz band broadens each landing point into a finite sea-surface intersection zone.
MU-A-2018-77845-017: Constant ship speed maps the four interval lengths to times whose sum is 46.20 h.
MU-A-2018-77845-018: Three controlled sweeps distinguish geometry-changing states from reflection-energy states and an unvisited F2-density region.

verification.summary: Equation 4 gives hj about 267.29 km and both adjacent Equation 3 branches about 3.692e11 m^-3, supporting near-continuity.
Figure 2 follows the expected lower refractive index at greater electron density and lower carrier frequency.
Figure 5 supports retaining the less angle-sensitive horizontal-polarization branch for later cases.
Figure 6 shows rho decreasing with angle and wind, with faster decline at higher frequency.
Figures 8-9 show the correction falling with angle, frequency, and Sh as Equation 12 predicts.
All four reported linear ratios equal 10^(Diff/10), confirming they are calm/turbulent.
All rugged/smooth ratios equal 10^(-Diff/10) and follow the printed Equation 12 trend.
Each Table 6 length equals right minus left and the four lengths sum to 1925 km.
Each time is length/41.67 km/h within rounding and the four times sum to 46.20 h.
Figure 15's near-zero F2-density response is reconciled with the path never reaching the perturbed upper region.
Figure 16 shows greater height increasing span/distance while retaining hop count in the displayed cases.
Figure 17 keeps path geometry fixed and adds larger reflection-loss steps with greater wind.

weaknesses.summary: Equation 12 prints exp(-g^2/2), while groundreflection.m prints exp(-1/(2g^2)); Table 5 follows the equation, not the code.
seareflection.m overwrites input v, uses an undefined index i, and overwrites fitted coefficients; the printed helper cannot directly reproduce wind-response results.
main.m selects parameterOcean(1), the calm horizontal coefficient, rather than rough coefficient index 3, so wind does not enter the printed multi-hop loss path.
The printed line assigning angled appears green/commented while later lines use angled, leaving executability dependent on lost PDF line/comment boundaries.
fcandMUF.m is called only by a test script; main.m does not gate frequencies with Equation 8.
Every F-layer loop exit is followed by mirrored descent, so the prose penetration branch is not implemented.
main.m hard-codes F_max=271.5 km, inconsistent with hj about 267.3 km and hmF2=339.3 km.

weaknesses.section: Latest reflection omitted from continuation state
weaknesses.summary: SrnLoop for the next while test is stored before the latest surface reflection loss is applied, potentially allowing an extra hop.
The outer loop includes NumLoop<=10 in addition to the stated 10 dB gate, but the prose does not disclose this second stopping rule.
Table 3 ratios are calm/turbulent and exceed one, whereas Figure 11 is turbulent/calm and Appendix A describes the opposite direction.
The four Table 6 zones have large gaps; summing 46.20 h does not establish uninterrupted reception.
Cartesian straight/mirrored paths omit Earth curvature while Table 4 reports propagation distances up to 14,650 km.
Figure 16 prose prints 289.8, 339.3, and 418.6 m, although Table 2, the plot axis, and ionosphere scale require km.
Equation 1 prints dB=km where the operational unit is dB/km.
The SNR ledger omits antenna gains, receive aperture, feeder loss, receiver noise figure, modulation requirement, and fading margin.
A single wet-concrete permittivity and conductivity are generalized to ground terrains without a material library or uncertainty range.
Wuhan/Sanya daytime-summer parameters are used without latitude, longitude, local time, solar activity, geomagnetic, or global calibration.
Figures 15-17 use a few one-factor curves with no joint uncertainty, confidence interval, error propagation, or observation-based calibration.
The ray paths and powers are not benchmarked against an independent ray tracer, ionosonde/IRI path observation, measured receive power, or sea-state dataset.
The PDF has a nearly blank physical page 10, 32 physical pages versus 30 internal pages, and a commercial watermark on every page.
Tables 3 and 5 label about 47 as Power(dBW), but Appendix B computes an SNR-like dB state; 47 dBW passive received power from a 100 W source is impossible.
Appendix B does not contain complete generating code for Tables 3-6 or Figures 11-17, so numerical provenance cannot be reproduced end to end.
The 1 km D/E step and 0.01 km F step are fixed without convergence, boundary-crossing, or error analysis.
Appendix A repeats the model claims, Figure 14, and Table 6; it is a communication artifact rather than corroborating evidence.
Several physical definitions rely on Wikipedia, Quora, and web pages; key relations should be checked against primary or standards sources.

Validate paths and powers against an independent ray tracer and measured ionosphere/receive data.

unresolved_questions.summary: Equation 12 prints exp(-g^2/2), while groundreflection.m prints exp(-1/(2g^2)); Table 5 follows the equation, not the code.
seareflection.m overwrites input v, uses an undefined index i, and overwrites fitted coefficients; the printed helper cannot directly reproduce wind-response results.
main.m selects parameterOcean(1), the calm horizontal coefficient, rather than rough coefficient index 3, so wind does not enter the printed multi-hop loss path.
The printed line assigning angled appears green/commented while later lines use angled, leaving executability dependent on lost PDF line/comment boundaries.
fcandMUF.m is called only by a test script; main.m does not gate frequencies with Equation 8.
Every F-layer loop exit is followed by mirrored descent, so the prose penetration branch is not implemented.
main.m hard-codes F_max=271.5 km, inconsistent with hj about 267.3 km and hmF2=339.3 km.
